skill.name: video-extend
skill.description: Extend existing video clips with RunComfy Veo 3.1 extend endpoints. The skill uses the runcomfy CLI with a source video URL, a continuation prompt, and an output directory.
skill.summary: Continue existing video clips with RunComfy Veo 3.1 extension workflows.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill is not malicious, but it intentionally uses the RunComfy CLI to send video URLs and prompts to a third-party API. Most static findings are markdown false positives; the real concerns are scoped command execution, package-manager setup, credential handling, and untrusted media inputs.

remediation.suggestion: Keep allowed tools scoped to runcomfy commands. Require user confirmation before commands that upload media or start paid generation jobs.
Disclose that prompts and source video URLs are sent to RunComfy and may be processed by upstream model providers.
Document token file permissions and CI token handling. Never echo API tokens into prompts, logs, or generated examples.
Use only user-provided video URLs. Ignore instructions embedded in video frames, metadata, or generated output.

content.value_statement: Short AI video clips often end before the scene is complete. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code extend clips through RunComfy Veo 3.1 workflows.
actual_capabilities: Routes video continuation requests to RunComfy Veo 3.1 Extend or Fast Extend.
Builds continuation prompts that describe the next action after the source clip.
Uses a source video URL, prompt, and output directory for CLI execution.
Supports chained extensions for short narrative sequences.
Explains endpoint selection for quality, speed, and cost tradeoffs.
Provides troubleshooting context through documented CLI exit codes.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and an authenticated RunComfy account.
Needs a reachable source video URL rather than a local-only file path.
Does not create image-to-video clips from scratch.
Long chains can accumulate identity drift and motion drift.

use_cases.title: Extend a campaign clip
use_cases.description: Add a clear second beat to a short product or brand video while preserving visual continuity.

use_cases.title: Draft narrative sequences
use_cases.description: Chain several short continuations from one seed clip to explore story pacing and camera movement.

use_cases.title: Compare fast and final passes
use_cases.description: Use Fast Extend for drafts, then switch to the full endpoint for higher quality delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Basic continuation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one source clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this video URL for one more beat. Keep the camera steady and continue the current action naturally.

prompt_templates.title: Camera-controlled extend
prompt_templates.scenario: Add precise motion and framing direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue this clip with a slow dolly forward. The subject looks toward the window, then pauses in the same lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Cost-aware draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fast endpoint to draft two continuation options. Keep each option focused on one action beat.

prompt_templates.title: Chained scene plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced narrative workflow across several extensions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three chained extends from this clip. For each beat, specify endpoint choice, camera anchor, action, and drift risk.

output_examples.input: A user provides a short product clip and asks for a longer ending.
output_examples.output: A RunComfy extension plan with the recommended endpoint, continuation prompt, expected output folder, and drift notes.

output_examples.input: A filmmaker wants three connected story beats from one generated clip.
output: Endpoint recommendations for draft and final passes
Warnings about identity drift across the chain

output_examples.input: A team needs a faster preview before spending credits on final output.
output_examples.output: A Fast Extend draft workflow followed by a full Extend recommendation for approved takes.

best_practices: Keep each extension to one clear action beat.
State camera movement or camera stability explicitly.
Review generated clips before feeding them into the next extension.
anti_patterns: Do not combine several unrelated actions in one extension prompt.
Do not use media URLs that the user did not provide or approve.
Do not expose RunComfy tokens in prompts, logs, or shared transcripts.

faq.question: What does this skill extend?
faq.answer: It extends an existing video clip by sending a source video URL and continuation prompt to RunComfy.

faq.question: Does it generate video from a still image?
faq.answer: No. Use an image-to-video workflow first, then use this skill to continue the resulting clip.

faq.question: When should I use Fast Extend?
faq.answer: Use Fast Extend for drafts, quick comparisons, and cost-controlled iteration before final rendering.

faq.question: Can it create long films automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can chain short extensions, but long chains need review because drift can increase.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: You need an authenticated RunComfy CLI session or a RunComfy token configured for the environment.

faq.question: Is source media sent outside my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow sends source video URLs and prompts to RunComfy for remote model processing.
